extracted.intended_audience: researchers and students in communication, political communication, and media studies (cross-national survey researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and measuring selective exposure and its correlates across different national political information environments using survey quasi-experiments, behavioral choice tasks, and composite country-level indicators of media fragmentation and polarization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective exposure (construct/definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendency to select information that is congenial to one’s own attitudes and social identities; the phenomenon under study that can be measured in multiple ways (self-reported, perceived, actual/behavioral).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses theoretical consequences (polarization, reduced cross-cutting discussion, lower tolerance) and positions selective exposure as affected by both individual predispositions and contextual features of political information environments (media fragmentation and polarization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-reported selective exposure (Tsfati-based scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: An 8-item self-report scale adapted from Tsfati (2016) measuring the tendency to select ideologically congruent political information; items rated on a 5-point Likert scale (1 = does not apply at all to 5 = absolutely applies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale reliability reported (Cronbach’s α = .839). Used as the most direct self-report measure of selective exposure and analyzed alongside other measures; see supplemental appendix for items. Interpret means and compare across countries; rescaled to 0–1 for comparability in cross-measure plots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived selective exposure (ideological distance index)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants rate all news outlets they use on a left–right ideological scale; outlet scores are subtracted from participants’ own self-placement and combined into a mean score index, with inversion so higher numbers indicate greater agreement between users and their media sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale composed of five items with high reliability (Cronbach’s α = .914). Captures users’ perceived consonance of their news diets with their own ideology; useful to contrast with self-report and behavioral measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actual selective exposure (behavioral choice metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavioral measure adapted from Knobloch-Westerwick and Meng (2009): participants choose articles from an online news magazine (8 articles on 4 topics) in wave 2; article choices are matched to prior attitudes and converted into a score = (consonant_count − dissonant_count) / total_articles_read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articles were pretested to be equally interesting and each had a clear stance. Participant attitudes collected on a 1–101 sliding scale in wave 1 to determine consonance. Positive scores indicate congruent selection. Use unobtrusive tracking; compare behavioral choice with self-report/perceived measures to detect discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media fragmentation — market size (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fragmentation indicator operationalized as media market size: proportion of population above 14 years that uses news regularly; larger markets permit more outlets and specialization, facilitating selective exposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Larger national media markets give space for partisan and niche outlets. Use established data sources (e.g., Reuters Digital News Report) to estimate regular news users; rank countries on this indicator when building comparative indices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media fragmentation — PSB share / non-PSB audience (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator using weekly audience share of public service broadcasting (PSB) versus non-PSB: a strong PSB share indicates a more saturated market and less fragmentation; low PSB share signals higher fragmentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use weekly audience share measures (e.g., Reuters Digital News Report) as proxy for PSB strength; interpret low PSB share as enabling more niche partisan offerings and higher fragmentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media fragmentation — non-shared news / shared news (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator based on the proportion of news users not using the main news media outlet (lack of shared news); higher non-shared news implies less common frames and greater fragmentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalize via average weekly usage share of the most-frequently used outlet; higher values of 'shared news' reduce fragmentation. Include online sources in the measure, not only PSB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media polarization — political parallelism (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Polarization indicator capturing media–party/political alignment: measured via constructs such as amount of commentary, partisan policy, journalists’ political orientation, media–party parallelism, political bias and PSB dependency (based on Brüggemann et al., 2014 / Hallin & Mancini).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multi-indicator operationalizations (journalists' orientations, content bias, media-party ties). Higher political parallelism indicates stronger ties between media outlets and political actors, facilitating attitude-consistent media selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media polarization — audience polarization (indicator)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicator capturing ideological extremity of media outlets' audiences: compute the average distance of the political orientation of audiences of the five most-used outlets per media type from the population mean; combine outlet extremity scores weighted by audience share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires audience-level ideological placement data per outlet; higher average divergence implies greater audience polarization across outlets. Use for cross-country comparisons to capture how ideologically clustered outlet audiences are.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined fragmentation–polarization index (country-level index)
rubrics_metrics.description: A composite index of five indicators (three fragmentation, two polarization): rank countries on each indicator, calculate mean rank score, and invert scores so higher numbers indicate higher fragmentation and polarization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines complementary indicators for greater explanatory power than single indicators. The study used ranks across five countries and inverted the mean score for interpretability (higher index = more fragmented/polarized).

rubrics_metrics.name: Media-type usage (predictor variables: TV, radio, newspaper, social media)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual-level dichotomous measures of whether participants used each media source type at least once in the past 7 days for political news (1 = use, 0 = no use).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as predictors of selective exposure in regressions. Hypotheses specified: H2 TV negative association with selective exposure; H3 radio negative; H4 newspapers positive; H5 social media positive. Allow multiple selections per participant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political interest (control variable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-reported general interest in politics measured on a 1–5 scale (1 = not at all interested to 5 = very interested).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include as a predictor/control because political interest correlates with news use patterns and selective exposure tendencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Left–right self-placement and political extremity
rubrics_metrics.description: Political orientation measured via an 11-point left–right self-placement scale (1 = clearly left to 11 = clearly right); extremity operationalized by folding the scale (distance from center).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both raw placement and extremity (folded) as predictors/controls; extremity often predicts stronger selective exposure behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: User socio-demographics (controls): sex, age, education
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard demographic controls: sex (male baseline), age (continuous), and education categorized into primary, secondary, tertiary due to cross-country differences in systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control for sociodemographics in regression models; education categorized to accommodate international comparisons (use ESS/NAES coding as references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral measure design principles (article selection task)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design considerations for the actual selective exposure task: include multiple topics, pretest topics and articles for equal interestingness, ensure clear pro/con stances, unobtrusive tracking of selections, and collect prior attitudes to match choices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pretest items to ensure parity in interest and clarity of stance. Use sliding-scale attitude measures to determine consonance. Compute normalized choice indices (e.g., difference/total read) to allow comparability across participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale reliability and measurement reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report internal consistency (Cronbach’s alpha) for multi-item scales (e.g., self-reported selective exposure α = .839; perceived selective exposure α = .914).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide means, SDs, and alpha coefficients. For comparability across measures, consider rescaling to common ranges (0–1) and reporting test–retest or wave reliability where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical approach and inferential procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ANCOVAs for cross-country comparisons, bootstrapped OLS regressions clustered on countries (1000 replications) to account for the small number of level-2 units, and Bonferroni-corrected post hoc tests for group comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When level-2 units (countries) are few, apply cluster bootstrapping (Huang, 2018) for robust inference. Report R2, unstandardized coefficients (B), standard errors, and significance levels; annotate p-value thresholds and use correction for multiple comparisons as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaling and comparability practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Rescale different selective exposure measures to a common 0–1 range for plotting and comparability across measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rescaling facilitates direct visual and statistical comparison of disparate measures (self-report, perceived, behavioral). Document rescaling procedure and ensure interpretability of transformed scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case selection rationale for cross-national comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Select countries to represent a spectrum of media fragmentation and polarization (here: Switzerland, Denmark = low; Poland, Italy, United States = higher), justifying choices by media market size, PSB strength, and evidence of partisan outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly justify country selection theoretically and with indicators; ensure variation on key country-level predictors to identify macro-level effects on individual selective exposure.
